lessons.title: If: -(으)면
lessons.learn: The all-round IF! 먹으면 (if I eat), 가면 (if I go), 비가 오면 (if it rains). Vowel-stems: -면, consonants: -으면! 와도 (even if): 와도 가요 = Even if it rains, I go!

grammar.title: -(으)면 (if) · -아/어도 (even if)
grammar.explain: 먹으면 (if eat), 가면 (if go). 비가 오면 안 가요 (if it rains, I won't go). 와도 가요 (even if rains, go)! 공부하면 알아요 (if you study, you know)!

examples.en: If it rains, I won't go.
Even if it rains, I'll go!

dialogue.en: If it rains tomorrow, what will you do?
Even if it rains, I'll go!

lessons.title: Let's and decisions: ㅂ시다/기로
lessons.learn: Formal LET'S! 갑시다 (let's go), 먹읍시다 (let's eat), 합시다! Decide: -기로 했어요 (I decided to): 가기로 했어요! Plans set: 예정이에요. Rally the group!

grammar.title: -(으)ㅂ시다 + -기로 했어요
grammar.explain: 갑시다! (let's go!), 먹읍시다! Plans decided: 한국에 가기로 했어요 (I decided to go to Korea). 예정: 갈 예정이에요 (scheduled to go)!

examples.en: I decided to go to Korea.

mistakes: Saying 가기로 해요 for past decisions — decided: 했어요!

dialogue.en: I decided to go to Seoul!

lessons.title: Full honorifics: -시-
lessons.learn: Honor in every verb! -시- infix: 가세요 (honorific go), 드세요 (honorific eat), 주무세요 (honorific sleep), 계세요 (honorific be). Honorific nouns: 말씀 (words), 성함 (name), 댁 (home)!

grammar.title: -시- infix + honorific nouns
grammar.explain: 선생님이 계세요? (Is the teacher there?). 잡수세요 = honorific eat (alt). 말씀하세요 (please speak, honored). Humble ME: 드리다 (I humbly give)!
grammar.pattern: -시- for elders · humble 드리다/저 for self
mistakes: Using -시- for YOURSELF — honorifics elevate OTHERS!
Saying 이름 to elders — their name: 성함!

lessons.title: Debate connectors
lessons.learn: Argue elegantly! 하지만 (but/however), 그래서 (so), 즉 (in other words), 예를 들어 (for example), 게다가 (besides), 결국 (after all). Chain: 예를 들어…게다가…그래서…!

grammar.title: Connector chains
grammar.explain: 지하철은 편리해요. 하지만 복잡해요. 즉, 좋아요! (The subway is handy. But crowded. In short, good!). Start sentences with 하지만/그래서/즉!

examples.en: The subway is handy. However, it's crowded.
In short, the subway is good!

mistakes: Saying 하지만 at sentence END — 하지만 starts sentences!

dialogue.en: The subway is handy. However, it's crowded.
In short, the subway is good!

lessons.title: Korean culture: 정 and food
lessons.learn: Culture time! 정 (deep affection/bond), 김치, 비빔밥, 한복 (traditional dress), 추석 (harvest festival). Have-tried: -아/어 봤어요: 김치를 먹어 봤어요? Guests first — 손님은 왕!

grammar.title: -아/어 봤어요: have tried
grammar.explain: 김치를 먹어 봤어요? (Have you tried kimchi?), 한복을 입어 봤어요 (I've tried hanbok)! 아/어 + 봤어요 = try-experience!
mistakes: Saying 먹은 봤어요 — try needs 아/어: 먹어 봤어요!
Saying 봤어요 for simple past — 봤어요 = tried/seen!

lessons.title: Storytelling: 옛날 옛적에
lessons.learn: Graduation! 옛날 옛적에 (long ago), 어느 날 (one day), 갑자기 (suddenly), 마침내 (at last), 마지막으로 (finally). Mix tenses: 갔어요, 먹고 있었어요, 먹고 싶어요! Tell YOUR Seoul story!

grammar.title: Story spine: 옛날 옛적에…마지막으로
grammar.explain: 옛날 옛적에…어느 날…갑자기…마침내…마지막으로 — the five-beat Korean story spine. Add 봤어요, 면, honorifics — graduate in style!
grammar.pattern: 옛날 옛적에 → 어느 날 → 갑자기 → 마지막으로

examples.en: Long ago, I went to Seoul.

mistakes: Starting tales with 어제 — stories open 옛날 옛적에!
Staying in 요-past only — mix 있었어요 + 싶어요!
